title: HCN2 fully rescues nicotine-induced brain malformations to control levels

fields.label: Label
fields.value: HCN2 fully rescues nicotine-induced brain malformations to control levels

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Injection of Hcn2-WT mRNA into nicotine-exposed Xenopus embryos reduced the incidence of major brain morphology defects from about 60% to about 6%, indistinguishable from untreated controls (about 7%).

fields.label: Work
fields.value: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Results › HCN2 rescues nicotine exposure-induced brain defects

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Remarkably, Hcn2-WT mRNA-injected embryos showed a complete rescue of brain morphology defects from nicotine exposure, to levels (~6%) indistinguishable from that of untreated control embryos (~7%) (Fig. 5f).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Pai VP, Pietak A, Willocq V, Ye B, Shi NQ, Levin M, “HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns”, Nature communications (2018), doi:10.1038/s41467-018-03334-5; section “Results › HCN2 rescues nicotine exposure-induced brain defects”. Scope: Xenopus laevis embryos exposed to nicotine (0.1 mg/mL, stages 10–35), injected with Hcn2-WT mRNA

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2018-hcn2-11: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.66

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The effect and proper equivalence criterion are highly operational. Published measurements can support a restricted check, but verifying complete rescue requires raw counts, batch structure, and a prespecified equivalence margin.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Reanalyse blinded embryo-level defect calls for untreated, nicotine, and nicotine-plus-HCN2 groups, testing both the reduction from about 60% to 6% and equivalence of rescue to the approximately 7% control level.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
No openly deposited embryo-level scores are identified.

Failure to reject a difference is not sufficient to establish equivalence.

discriminating power: 0.9

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The three percentages and the indistinguishability claim are a straightforward contingency-table test. Those counts were not deposited, and the data statement does not point to a repository. Re-reading Figure 5f repeats the claim rather than testing it. The design would discriminate rescue from a partial improvement once the individual outcomes exist.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Count major brain-morphology defects at stage 45 in untreated controls, nicotine (0.1 mg/mL, stages 10–35), and nicotine plus Hcn2-WT mRNA. Rescue to control levels is confirmed if nicotine is near 60% and the HCN2 arm is statistically indistinguishable from the ~7% control; a residual elevation in the HCN2 arm would refute complete rescue.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The bar graph is not accompanied by an open embryo-level table.

Major-defect categories can be scored differently by another observer.

Injection and nicotine timing have to match the stated window.
